Gori Shankar R/o Village Suraya Ps- Leyka Zila Firozabad, U.P. ............Driver/Respondent no. 1 2. Kumar Siddinath S/o Sh. Kapeel Dev Pandey R/o H.No. Y-38, Ground Floor, Sec.-12, Noida, U.P. ............ Owner/Respondent no. 2 Mact No.:393/20 Anil Kumar v. Pramod Kumar Page No. 1 of 26 Bk 3. M/s Universal Sompo Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd. Ground Floor, Plot no.52, Block-B, Sec.-44, Gurgaon, Haryana. .......Insurance Company/Respondent no. 3 Date of accident : 09.01.2020 Date of filing of Dar : 03.12.2020 Date of Decision : 24.02.2023 Award 1.
texts.facts: In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act on 03.12.2020 and same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. On 03.10.2020 victim Anil Kumar gave his statement to the police and as per his statement, on 09.01.2020, he was driving his TSR bearing no. DL 1RQ 7509 and going towards Badarpur with passengers from AIIMS Hospital. At about 11.30 PM, when the he reached Mathura Road, Sukhdev Vihar, Gate no.2, a dumper bearing no. HR 38S 2480 hit against his TSR from the back side which caused damage to his TSR and physical injuries to the victim. It is further stated that initially driver of the offending vehicle/truck came down from his offending vehicle and assured the victim that he will get him medically treated. But later he escaped from there after leaving such offending vehicle on the spot. The crowd gathered over there and someone called at 100 number and one person in a car from the crowd took the injured to hospital. It is further stated MACT No.:393/20 Anil Kumar v. Pramod Kumar Page No. 2 of 26 BK that passenger of his TSR suffered minor injury only and they left for their home. It is further stated that driver and owner of such vehicle did not pay for the medical expenses of such victim/claimant. Therefore, later on, on 03.10.2020, victim lodged present complaint. 3. It is further claimed by concerned police station on 09.01.2020 itself, HC Nawal Singh No. 3404/South-East was assigned DD no. 7A regarding such accident but he found victim left the hospital. Further, vide DD no.10A received from Apollo hospital with MLC no. 38/22 regarding patient Anil Kumar S/o Ram Surat Singh and as per such MLC, injury was grievous. It is further stated that such victim was in touch with the police official but he did not got registered his statement. 4. Thus, despite such specific information regarding occurrence of crime with documents relating to the same, it appears that concerned SHO at that time of 09.01.2020 as well as such police official Nawal Singh slept over the matter and did not register the FIR under appropriate offences despite clear mandate under section 154 Cr.P.C. 5. Thereafter, only after nine months on 03.10.2020 when such victim appeared before the police official, his statement was recorded. Thus, by such conduct the whole purpose of DAR system (according to which DAR was to be filed within ninety days), which is timely compensation to the victim is frustrated by such inaction by concerned police officials. 6. As such, a copy of this order be sent to DCP MACT No.:393/20 Anil Kumar v. Pramod Kumar Page No. 3 of 26 BK concerned for action against such concerned SHO at the time of accident of 09.01.2020 and HC Nawal Singh. 7. But in any case, after the investigation chargesheet is prepared on 17.11.2020 and filed u/s 279, 338 IPC against the R-1. Further, present DAR also filed. 8. Further, as per record, R-1 & 2 filed their reply to DAR and it is stated that the DAR filed by police is false and frivolous. That the entire contents and allegations of the DAR filed by the police are denied and no alleged accident has been caused from the vehicle of driver and they have been falsely implicated in the present case. It is further stated that in any case offending vehicle was inured with R-3/insurance company. Anil Kumar vs . Pramod Kumar on 24 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184454959/ 2 9. Further, reply/report filed by insurance company and in a nutshell, it is stated that there is delay in lodging the FIR and that the alleged accident has taken place due to sole carelessness and negligence of the claimant. That the involvement of vehicle no. HR 38S 2480 (Truck) is specifically denied. It is further claimed that there is contributory negligence in any case of 50% of the victim himself. 10. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed by my Ld. Predecessor of this Tribunal on 17.09.2021: 1. OPP. 2. MACT No.:393/20 Anil Kumar v. Pramod Kumar Page No. 4 of 26 BK 3. Relief. 11. As per record, injured Anil Kumar Singh examined himself as PW-1. Such PW1 tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/1. He relied upon various documents as Ex. PW-1/A to Ex. PW-1/G (colly) and Mark-A including relating to his identity and medical treatment and bills. 12. He was cross-examined by learned counsel for insurance company/R-3 as well as R-1 & 2. 13. No other evidence has been led on behalf of petitioner.
texts.arguments: Including in the case of Bimla Devi & Ors vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors [(2009) 13 SC 530,[ in Kaushnumma Begum and others v/s New India Assurance Company Limited, [2001 ACJ 421 SC[, in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana cited as [2009 ACJ 287], it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court/ Hon'ble High Court that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of MACT No.:393/20 Anil Kumar v. Pramod Kumar Page No. 5 of 26 BK Anil Kumar vs . Pramod Kumar on 24 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184454959/ 3 Including in the case of National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it has been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court and Hon'ble High Court that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 19. It may further be noted that including in the case of Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it is held by Hon'ble Supreme Court/ Hon'ble High Court that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. Issue no. 2 27. At this stage, before proceeding further, by rely upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC, it can be noted that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of MACT No.:393/20 Anil Kumar v. Pramod Kumar Page No. 8 of 26 BK wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. 28. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) Anil Kumar vs . Pramod Kumar on 24 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184454959/ 5 (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii) (a) and (iv). 28.2. . It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). 28.7. It may be noted that in the judgment of Ram Charan & Ors. Vs. The New India Assurance Co. Ltd., MAC Appeal no. 433/2013, decided on 18.10.2022 it was noted regarding rate of interest: "25 to evaluate the submission made by counsel for the applicants, it is imperative to examine the guiding principles for the grant of interest. , the following was held while interpreting section 171 of the MV Act, 1988:- Three decisions were cited before us by Mr. A. P. Mohanty, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Appellant, in support of his contentions. Interest is compensation for forbearance or detention of money and that interest being MACT No.:393/20 Anil Kumar v. Pramod Kumar Page No. 17 of 26 BK awarded to a party only for being kept out of the money which ought to have been paid to him. In other matters, awarding of interest depends upon the statutory provisions mercantile usage and doctrine of equity. 42. Having regard to the prevailing rate of interest and the judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, including in the case of Erudhaya Priya vs State Express Transport decided on 27 July, 2020, Civil Appeal Nos. 2811-2812 OF 2020 [Arising out of SLP (C) Nos.8495-8496 of 2018], which is three Judges Bench judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court, such interest @ 9% per annum is deemed fit and accordingly granted in the present case. 43. The total compensation payable to the claimant would be Rs.16,04,731/- with simple interest at the rate of 9% p.a. from the date of filing of DAR till its actual realization. Anil Kumar vs . Pramod Kumar on 24 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184454959/ 11 LIABILITY:- 44. The State Bank of India, Saket Courts, Delhi is directed to disburse the amount in accordance with MACAD formulated by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi. ......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". Anil Kumar v. Pramod Kumar Page No. 22 of 26 BK noted that in present case, accused suffered injury and incurred expenses including on medical expenses, special diet, conveyance.
